question: What exactly is the treatment when the same model runs through different harnesses?
intended_takeaway: Report locked model–harness–environment candidates, not a model leaderboard.
out_of_scope: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

placement.what_to_watch: See how candidate identity, paired assignment, ordering, and reporting rules prevent a harness comparison from becoming a model leaderboard.

claims.claim: One model can produce several behavioral candidates.
support: Harness, environment, tools, and stopping policy change observable behavior.
The model name alone is not the reporting unit.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: Four harnesses receive the same two locked task coordinates.
support: GLM-5.2, context, local Docker, and one attempt stay fixed.
A missing task–harness coordinate remains missing.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: Lock and record one deterministic serial expansion.
support: The canary uses one worker, one seed, and an inspectable cell order.
Reproducible ordering does not estimate away temporal noise.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: Compare aligned candidate rows under locked conditions.
support: Raw task contrasts belong to model–harness–environment candidates.
Two tasks and one attempt do not estimate a stable harness ranking.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: A reversal is a result, not a reason to pool.
support: A harness can lead on one locked task and trail on the other.
Separate task rows preserve the discordance.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: Protocol differences can prevent a pure harness claim.
support: If adapters or tool semantics differ, report the full candidates.
Do not subtract away behavior-changing preparation.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: No difference and harness reversal are both publishable outcomes.
support: The design is useful even when there is no winner.
Incomplete infrastructure can still make the study uninterpretable.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.

claims.claim: Harness identity belongs inside experimental design.
support: It travels with the candidate through execution and evidence.
The final claim remains bounded to that locked system.
claims.caveat: The preregistration contains no observed winner or causal harness result.
